title: Cloudflare Workers MCP: How to Build a Remote Server
summary: Cloudflare workers MCP allows developers to deploy model context protocol servers directly to edge networks for reduced latency.
body_markdown:
## How Cloudflare Workers host MCP servers


A persistent, globally accessible endpoint is provided by Cloudflare Workers, allowing Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers to communicate with remote AI clients using standardized web protocols.


### The SSE transport protocol explained


Server-Sent Events (SSE) are the primary transport layer for remote MCP implementations. They allow a Cloudflare Worker to maintain a unidirectional stream of data to the LLM client over standard HTTPS.


The Worker uses SSE to push tool execution results and context updates to the client without the overhead of maintaining a two-way WebSocket connection.


Structured data is received as a continuous stream by the LLM client under this architecture. The client doesn't wait for a single, bulky HTTP response that might time out during complex database queries.


### Connecting Claude and ChatGPT to the edge


Frontier models can now call tools hosted on Cloudflare’s infrastructure because leading AI interfaces support remote MCP endpoints.


Claude Desktop connects via a configuration file that points to a local bridge or proxy script, which relays requests to the Worker’s URL. This allows the model to pull in real-time data from external repositories.


Because Claude Desktop currently only supports local stdio communication, you must use a local bridge or proxy script to translate the desktop client's stdio commands into the Worker's SSE format.


This bridge acts as a lightweight intermediary that allows the local application to communicate with the remote edge environment.


### Setting up a local MCP bridge with Node.js


The bridge is typically a Node.js script that runs on your machine to relay messages between the local Claude app and the remote Worker. You can use community tools like` mcp-proxy` or the official` sse-client` examples found in the MCP TypeScript SDK repository.


To start the bridge, you run a command such as` npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector sse <YOUR_WORKER_URL>` in your terminal. This command creates a local stdio interface that you then link in your Claude Desktop configuration file, effectively routing your local agent's requests to the global edge.


### Configuring Claude Desktop for your MCP server


Running the bridge command generates a local transport address that the AI agent needs to recognize. You must manually add this command to your Claude Desktop configuration file, typically located at` ~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json` on macOS or the equivalent AppData path on Windows.


Inside the mcpServers object of this file, you define a new entry where the command is` npx` and the arguments include the full inspector or proxy string.


This step is what finally tells the local AI agent to route its tool requests through the bridge to your Cloudflare Worker.


GPT-6 Astra uses remote tool definitions to trigger the Worker. Gemini 4 Carbon interfaces with the Worker to execute complex reasoning tasks against proprietary datasets that the model's training set doesn't include.


### Securing API keys with Cloudflare Workers secrets


Sensitive credentials are managed through encrypted environment variables within Cloudflare Workers.


The architecture prevents API keys for services like GitHub or Stripe from being exposed to the LLM client. The AI model only sees the final output of the tool, so the underlying authentication tokens remain strictly within the Cloudflare sandbox.


The Worker only executes pre-defined, scoped logic. You can rotate these secrets within the Cloudflare Dashboard to instantly revoke access across all distributed edge nodes without redeploying the MCP server code.
